Starlink is one of the most useful pieces of tech on the planet right now.

Most people don't know it was built to fund Mars and proved its worth in a war.

The origin: January 2015, Elon Musk stood in a Seattle warehouse with 60 engineers and described a satellite internet project. He wasn't trying to build an internet company. He was trying to generate the revenue SpaceX needed to get to Mars.

The graveyard: two companies had already tried LEO internet. Teledesic, backed by Bill Gates, shut down without launching a single operational satellite. Iridium filed for bankruptcy after spending $5 billion. The industry had written LEO internet off as economically impossible.

The unlock: SpaceX solved reusable rockets first. When launch costs dropped by 10x, the economics that killed every previous attempt stopped being a problem.

The proof: February 2022. Russia invades Ukraine. Starlink terminals arrive within 48 hours. Ukrainian forces use them to keep communications alive in a war where the enemy was destroying every other option. The world realizes what had been quietly built.

The outcome today:

~ 12 million subscribers across 150 countries
~ 37 major airlines
~ US military backbone
~ Remote farms, disaster zones, polar routes, ocean crossings

It started as a Mars fundraiser. It survived a graveyard. It proved itself in a war.

Now it's just the internet. For everyone.
